output.summary: A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to western Europe, found in ditches, streams, and fresh or brackish wetlands. Its hollow stems root where nodes touch the ground, and crushed leaves smell of carrot. Traditionally harvested in several Mediterranean countries, its young leaves and tender shoots are eaten raw, boiled, or as a condiment, though it can be confused with allegedly poisonous lesser water parsnip.
